Note 1 - Organization and Business Operations
text: NOTE 1 — ORGANIZATION AND BUSINESS OPERATIONS

Northern Minerals & Exploration Ltd. (the “Company”) is a natural resource company operating in oil and gas production in central Texas and Oklahoma and exploration for gold and silver in northern Nevada.

The Company was incorporated in Nevada on December 11, 2006 under the name Punchline Entertainment, Inc. On August 22, 2012, the Company’s board of directors approved an agreement and plan of merger to effect a name change of the Company from Punchline Entertainment, Inc. to Punchline Resources Ltd. On July 12, 2013, the stockholders approved an amendment to change the name of the Company from Punchline Resources Ltd. to Northern Minerals & Exploration Ltd. FINRA approved the name change on August 13, 2013.
On November 22, 2017, the Company created a wholly owned subsidiary, Kathis Energy LLC (Kathis”) for the purpose of conducting oil and gas drilling programs in Texas.
On December 14, 2017, Kathis Energy, LLC and other Limited Partners, created Kathis Energy Fund 1, LP, a limited partnership created for raising investor funds.

On May 7, 2018, the Company created ENMEX LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary in Mexico, for the purposes of managing and operating its investments in Mexico including but not limited to the Joint Venture opportunity being negotiated with Pemer Bacalar on the 61 acres on the Bacalar Lagoon on the Yucatan Peninsula. There was no activity from inception to date.

notes.title: Note 2 - Significant Accounting Policies
text: NOTE 2 — SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES
Basis of presentation

These financial statements have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (“US GAAP”) and the rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”).
Use of estimates

The preparation of financial statements in conformity with generally accepted accounting principles requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements and the reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting period. Actual results may differ from those estimates.
Cash and Cash Equivalents

The Company considers all cash accounts, which are not subject to withdrawal restrictions or penalties, and all highly liquid debt instruments purchased with a maturity of three months or less as cash and cash equivalents. The carrying amount of financial instruments included in cash and cash equivalents approximates fair value because of the short maturity for the instruments held. The Company had no cash equivalents as of July 31, 2026 and 2025.
Principles of Consolidation

The accompanying consolidated financial statements include the accounts of the Company and its wholly-owned subsidiaries, Kathis Energy LLC, Kathis Energy Fund 1, LP and Enmex Operations LLC. All financial information has been prepared in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America. All significant intercompany transactions and balances have been eliminated.
Mineral Property Acquisition and Exploration Costs

Mineral property acquisition and exploration costs are expensed as incurred until such time as economic reserves are quantified. Cost of lease, exploration, carrying and retaining unproven mineral lease properties are expensed as incurred. We have chosen to expense all mineral exploration costs as incurred given that it is still in the exploration stage. Once our company has identified proven and probable reserves in its investigation of its properties and upon development of a plan for operating a mine, it would enter the development stage and capitalize future costs until production is established. When a property reaches the production stage, the related capitalized costs will be amortized over the estimated life of the probable-proven reserves. When our company has capitalized mineral properties, these properties will be periodically assessed for impairment of value and any diminution in value.

notes.title: Note 3 - Going Concern
text: NOTE 3 — GOING CONCERN

The accompanying consolidated financial statements have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (“U.S. GAAP”), which contemplate the continuation of the Company as a going concern and the realization of assets and satisfaction of liabilities in the normal course of business.

For the year ended July 31, 2026, the Company incurred a net loss of $474,918 and used $283,432 in cash from operating activities. As of July 31, 2026, the Company had an accumulated deficit of $4,396,713, a working capital deficit of $251,303, and cash of $10,488. The Company has incurred recurring operating losses and has limited financial resources available to fund its ongoing operations and contractual obligations. These conditions raise substantial doubt about the Company's ability to continue as a going concern within one year after the date the financial statements are issued.

Management intends to address these conditions by seeking additional financing through the issuance of equity securities, debt financing arrangements, and other available sources of capital. The Company also intends to continue generating revenue from its existing oil and gas production activities while managing operating expenditures and pursuing opportunities to improve its financial position. However, there can be no assurance that the Company will be successful in obtaining sufficient additional financing or generating adequate cash flows from operations to meet its obligations as they become due.

Management's plans have not alleviated the substantial doubt regarding the Company's ability to continue as a going concern. The accompanying consolidated financial statements have been prepared assuming the Company will continue as a going concern and do not include any adjustments to the carrying amounts or classification of assets and liabilities that might be necessary if the Company is unable to continue operations.

On June 2, 2026, the Company entered into a Memorandum of Understanding with R.A. Miller Energy, Inc. ("RAM") regarding the acquisition of a 5.4165 net mineral acre leasehold interest located in Sections 27 and 34, Township 2 North, Range 3 West, and Section 3, Township 1 North, Range 3 West, Garvin County, Oklahoma, associated with the proposed Bosworth 0203 1H-27X well.

Pursuant to the agreement, the Company agreed to acquire the leasehold interest for total consideration of $21,666, consisting of (i) $10,833 in cash payable on or before July 31, 2026, and (ii) $10,833 payable in 216,660 shares of the Company’s common stock. The shares were valued at $18,394 based on the closing market price of $0.0849 per share on June 2, 2026. Of this amount, $10,833 was recorded as a prepaid acquisition cost, and the remaining $7,561 was recognized as an expense. The acquisition of the leasehold interest has been delayed pending verification of certain matters necessary to complete the transaction. As of the date of this report, the $10,833 cash payment due on July 31, 2026, has not been made, and the transaction remains pending. Given the uncertainty surrounding the completion of the acquisition, the Company has not recorded a liability for the unpaid cash consideration pending further evaluation of the status and enforceability of the agreement.

notes.title: Note 5 - Supplemental Oil and Gas Information
text: N OTE 5 — SUPPLEMENTAL OIL AND GAS INFORMATION
The Company provides supplemental oil and gas information in accordance with ASC 932, Extractive Activities — Oil and Gas .

As of July 31, 2026, the Company's oil and gas properties had a carrying value of $0 following the recognition of impairment losses. Based on the Company's most recent reserve evaluation, no proved oil and gas reserves were reported as of July 31, 2026. Accordingly, the standardized measure of discounted future net cash flows attributable to proved reserves was $0 at July 31, 2026.

Notwithstanding the absence of reported proved reserves, the Company's wells remain operational and continue to produce oil and natural gas. The Company expects to continue recognizing revenue from production activities as oil and natural gas are sold. Future production and revenues will depend on actual well performance, commodity prices, and operating conditions.
The standardized measure and PV-10 values presented are not intended to represent the fair value of the Company’s reserves.
Standardized Measure of Discounted Future Net Cash Flows

The standardized measure of discounted future net cash flows relating to the Company’s proved reserves as of July 31, 2025 is presented below. The estimates are based on the 12-month average of the first-day-of-the-month prices for oil and natural gas, held constant throughout the life of the properties, and current cost estimates as of each year-end. The future net cash flows are discounted at 10 percent per annum as required by GAAP.

notes.title: Note 6 - Crypto Assets (Bitcoin)
text: NOTE 6 — CRYPTO ASSETS (BITCOIN)

During January 2026, the Company acquired 0.50096 Bitcoin for investment purposes. The Company accounts for its Bitcoin holdings in accordance with ASC 350, Intangibles — Goodwill and Other , as amended by ASU 2023-08, Accounting for and Disclosure of Crypto Assets . Under this guidance, Bitcoin is measured at fair value at each reporting date, with changes in fair value recognized in earnings.
The Company determines the fair value of Bitcoin using quoted market prices in active markets for identical assets, which are classified as Level 1 inputs under ASC 820, Fair Value Measurement .

As of July 31, 2026, the Company held 0.50096 Bitcoin with a fair value of $31,476. During the year ended July 31, 2026, the Company recognized an unrealized loss of $10,663 resulting from changes in the fair value of Bitcoin, which is included in other income (expense) in the consolidated statements of operations.

notes.title: Note 7 - Loans Payable
text: NOTE 7 — LOANS PAYABLE

On April 16, 2017, the Company executed a promissory note for $15,000 with a third party. The note matured in two years and interest is set at $3,000 for the full two years. As of July 31, 2026, there is $15,000 and $12,375 of principal and accrued interest, respectively, due on this loan. As of July 31, 2025, there was $15,000 and $10,875 of principal and accrued interest, respectively, due on this loan. This loan is currently in default.

During the year ended July 31, 2020, a third party loaned the Company $60,000. The loan was unsecured, bears interest at 8% per annum and matured on September 1, 2021. On April 30, 2025, the Company and the third party entered into a debt settlement agreement, whereby the parties agreed to settle the outstanding principal and interest for $30,000 in cash and 1,137,900 shares of common stock at $0.05 per share.
As of July 31, 2026 and 2025, the Company owes a third party $23,500 and $23,500, respectively. The loan is unsecured, non-interest bearing and due on demand.

On June 1, 2023, the Company entered into a settlement and promissory note agreement with Golden Sands Exploration Inc. (“Golden Sands”) to settle an outstanding obligation of $285,453 arising from a default under a property option agreement. Under the settlement, Golden Sands agreed to reduce the obligation to $85,000, bearing interest at 6% per annum, with a maturity date of June 1, 2026.

On May 26, 2026, the Company and Golden Sands executed an amended agreement extending the repayment terms through June 1, 2027, and increasing the annual interest rate to 8%, effective June 1, 2026. Under the amended agreement, the Company agreed to pay $1,275 of previously accrued interest by June 1, 2026, followed by principal payments of $20,000 on each of August 15, 2026, December 1, 2026, and March 1, 2027, with the remaining $25,000 due June 1, 2027. Accrued interest is payable with each principal installment. The Company may prepay the obligation at any time without penalty. All other terms of the original agreement remain in effect.

As of July 31, 2026, there is $85,000 and $1,134 of principal and accrued interest, respectively, due on this loan. As of July 31, 2025, there is $85,000 and $850 of principal and accrued interest, respectively, due on this loan.

notes.title: Note 9 - Related Party Note Payable
text: NOTE 9 — RELATED PARTY NOTE PAYABLE

On January 31, 2025, the Company entered into a convertible secured promissory note with Victor Miranda providing for a line of credit (“LOC”) of up to $500,000. The agreement consolidated a previously issued unsecured promissory note of $25,000 into the new secured obligation. The note bears interest at 5% per annum and matures on January 31, 2027. The Company may prepay the note at any time without penalty.

At the lender's option, outstanding principal, accrued interest, and other amounts due may be converted into shares of the Company's common stock at a conversion price of $0.05 per share, subject to adjustment. The note is secured by collateral pursuant to a separate security agreement. Upon an event of default, the interest rate increases to the lesser of 18% per annum or the maximum rate permitted by law, and the lender may accelerate repayment of the outstanding balance.

The convertible promissory note contains a full-ratchet anti-dilution provision that provides for a downward adjustment to the conversion price if the Company subsequently issues common stock or certain convertible securities at a price below the then-effective conversion price, subject to specified exceptions. During the years ended July 31, 2026 and 2025, the Company did not issue any securities that triggered an adjustment to the conversion price. Accordingly, the conversion price remained at $0.05 per share as of July 31, 2026.

On May 29, 2026, Mr. Miranda converted $402,000 and $12,942 of principal and interest into 8,298,833, pursuant to the terms of the LOC. As of July 31, 2026, there is $65,000 and $331 of principal and accrued interest, respectively, due on the LOC. As of July 31, 2025, there is $135,000 and $2,040 of principal and accrued interest, respectively, due on the LOC.

notes.title: Note 11 - Operating Segments
text: NOTE 11 — OPERATING SEGMENTS

The Company operates as one reportable segment, consisting primarily of oil and natural gas production and mineral exploration activities. The Company determines its operating segments based on the manner in which its Chief Operating Decision Maker (“CODM”) evaluates financial performance and allocates resources. The Company's Chief Executive Officer serves as the CODM.

The CODM reviews the Company's consolidated financial results, including revenues, operating expenses, and net income (loss), to assess performance, monitor operating costs, and make decisions regarding the allocation of resources. The Company uses consolidated net income (loss) as its measure of segment profit or loss.

notes.title: Note 12 - Income Tax
text: NOTE 12 — INCOME TAX

Deferred taxes are provided on a liability method whereby deferred tax assets are recognized for deductible temporary differences and operating loss and tax credit carry forwards and deferred tax liabilities are recognized for taxable temporary differences. Temporary differences are the differences between the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and their tax bases. Deferred tax assets are reduced by a valuation allowance when, in the opinion of management, it is more likely than not that some portion or all of the deferred tax assets will not be realized. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are adjusted for the effects of changes in tax laws and rates on the date of enactment. The U.S. federal income tax rate of 21% is being used.

At July 31, 2026, the Company had net operating loss carry forwards of approximately $1,069,000 that maybe offset against future taxable income. No tax benefit has been reported in the July 31, 2026 or 2025 financial statements since the potential tax benefit is offset by a valuation allowance of the same amount.

On December 22, 2017, the U.S. government enacted comprehensive tax legislation commonly referred to as the Tax Cut and Jobs Act (the “Tax Act”). The Tax Act establishes new tax laws that affects 2018 and future years, including a reduction in the U.S. federal corporate income tax rate to 21% effective January 1, 2018, for certain deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities.

Due to the change in ownership provisions of the Tax Reform Act of 1986, net operating loss carry forwards for Federal income tax reporting purposes are subject to annual limitations. Should a change in ownership occur, net operating loss carry forwards may be limited as to use in future years.

ASC Topic 740 provides guidance on the accounting for uncertainty in income taxes recognized in a company’s financial statements. Topic 740 requires a company to determine whether it is more likely than not that a tax position will be sustained upon examination based upon the technical merits of the position. If the more-likely-than-not threshold is met, a company must measure the tax position to determine the amount to recognize in the financial statements.
